subject: Simple ODE code for multiple dosing setting

messages.author: ed404d405a3e6877
messages.subject: Simple ODE code for multiple dosing setting
parts:
Dear Stan Developers,
 
I am experimenting with the ODE solvers in Stan. I managed to simulate data governed by a simple first order ODE with a goal to extend the stan code to real PK and Toxicology problems. Currently I am able to simulate data with a single initial dose. However, I would like to implement multiple dosing regimen, as described here (https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/ODE-Integrator-Support)
 
"Dosing: discontinous inputs to the differential equation in the form of "dosing". For example, a drug is injected into a tissue, and complete diffusion is assumed, so it looks like a discontinuous jump."
 
I include the stan code and the R code to run it. I also included the plot of the results from R 'deSolve' package. These are what I would like to reproduce in Stan.
 
Many thanks in advance,
Shamil.

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: Simple ODE code for multiple dosing setting
parts:
Hi!

Things are quit tedious under Stan at the moment concerning multiple dosing: You have to stop the ODE inegrator each time you want to inject a new dose. The Stan ODE integrator cannot handle events which is why you have to manually stop the ODE at each dosing time-point (then add the dose and restart). It works, but is tedious; hopefully we get this event handling at some point in Stan directly.

Best,
Sebastian

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Simple ODE code for multiple dosing setting
parts:
If you have initial state y(t = 0), observation times t[1] through t[10]
with a dose delta_y at t[5], then you run the integrator with initial
state y(t=0) for times t[1] through t[5], get the value for y out of the
result for t[5], add the dose delta_y, then integrate with that as the initial
condition for times t[6] through t[10].

- Bob

messages.author: ed404d405a3e6877
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Simple ODE code for multiple dosing setting
parts:
Hi Bob,
 
Thanks for clarifying. The y in the error message is not the variable y in my model - that was the confusing part. After some tinkering with the data structures in stan, I finally managed to implement the multiple dosing ODE model (see code below). Is there a more efficient way of using stan data structures to produce the same result?
 

ode_stan2 <- '
functions {
   real[] ode1( real t
               , real[] y
               , real[] ke
               , real[] x_r
               , int[] x_i) {
         real dydt[1];
            dydt[1] <-  -ke[1] * y[1];
            return dydt;
                            }
}
data {
   int T_dose;  // number of evaluations (ts) during each dosing period
   int ndose;
   int T;
   real y0[1];
   real t0;
   real tsm[ndose, T_dose];    // matrix of time points - each row corresponds to a new dosing interval
   real ke[1];
   real vdose[ndose];
}
transformed data {
   real x_r[0];
   int x_i[0];
}
parameters {
 
}
model {
}
generated quantities {
   vector[T_dose] y_hat[ndose];
   real y_res[T_dose, 1];
   real y_ini[1];
   real ts[T_dose];
   real t0j;
// Until second dose:
   y_ini[1] <- y0[1] + vdose[1];       // initial concentration + first dose at time = 0, if any
   ts <- tsm[1];
   y_res  <- integrate_ode(ode1, y_ini, t0, ts, ke, x_r, x_i);
   y_hat[1] <- to_vector(to_matrix(y_res));
 
// After second dose:
   for (j in 2:ndose) {
          y_ini[1] <- y_hat[j - 1, T_dose] + vdose[j];
          ts <- tsm[j];
          t0j <- tsm[j, 1] - 0.0000001;
          y_res  <- integrate_ode(ode1, y_ini, t0j, ts, ke, x_r, x_i);
          y_hat[j] <- to_vector(to_matrix(y_res));
    }
}
'
Best,
Shamil.
